summary: A pack is a reusable canonical library entity shared with character sprite assets. PackBody has a library name, optional shelf brief, a SpritePackValue and optional named groups. The schema owns its types, while this reference explains field meaning and embeds generated field tables. The image-pack adapter imports a supported raster image or a ZIP of supported pictures and sounds, and writes ZIP output. Imported filenames are recorded in original metadata; the original ZIP container is not retained. Media lives in canonical item refs, which may be inline data or references to stored assets. Studio-created packs begin without imported escrow. SpritePackValue defines item identities, labels, media references, optional MIME types, a pack-wide enabled flag and a default face. Character media and standalone packs use the same hub shape. Audio items use the larger media cap and bounded Range serving. The page distinguishes canonical media from source-container escrow and avoids claiming byte-identical ZIP output.

sections.title: How to read the field table
sections.summary: The field table is generated from schema documentation by scripts/docs-fields.ts and embedded verbatim. Changes belong in schema comments followed by regeneration. Field names mark optional entries with a question mark, and types come from TypeScript. Producers names formats declared by each field comment; a dash means no field-specific producer is listed. It does not mean the image-pack adapter cannot create the entity from supported files. Meaning describes each field, while broader explanations remain in surrounding prose. No table cell is maintained independently.

sections.title: Composition
sections.summary: PackBody stays flat with name optional shelf brief the pack SpritePackValue and optional groups map of named SpritePackValue entries. There are no always-present sub-objects like CharacterBody eight groups. pack and each groups entry share SpritePackValue the label-to-image hub that character media.assets role emotion also project through. SpritePackValue and SpritePackItem live in src/core/media/pack.ts not pack schema so docs-fields does not generate their table; prose covers them under The sprite pack hub shape. The body table comes from docs/generated/fields.pack.md.

sections.title: Pack body
sections.summary: PackBody fields: name is the library and tab name. brief is a short shelf card blurb never host wire. pack is the emotion pack as SpritePackValue label to image hub shared with character media. groups is optional Record string SpritePackValue for per-character groups where the flat pack is the default group when groups is absent.

sections.title: The sprite pack hub shape
sections.summary: SpritePackValue in core media pack.ts is the label-to-image hub for character cards and library packs. items is SpritePackItem array of id label ref and optional mime. enabled is pack-wide on off. defaultLabel picks the resting face; resolvePackFace falls back to neutral then the first item. packFromMedia and emotionAssetsFromPack convert character media.assets role emotion through this shape. groups holds one SpritePackValue per named member. An item whose mime is audio is a sound file the Stage wing's Music tab plays: held to the 32 MiB media cap, served with Range support cut from one bounded read, shown as a note glyph, printed under the same cap and imported back byte for byte from a zip.

sections.title: What rides escrow, not a field
sections.summary: The image-pack adapter records imported member filenames in the original entry. It converts media bytes into canonical item references and does not retain the ZIP container. Studio-created packs still begin as bare canonical entities without original metadata. Imported escrow is therefore descriptive filename metadata, not a saved source archive or a promise of byte-identical ZIP output. Inline data URIs and asset-store references hold the media itself; they are not separate binary source carriers beside canonical fields. The source filenames describe the import only.

sections.title: See also
sections.summary: The architecture reference explains the canonical wrapper, adapter contract and escrow rules. The character entity Media section describes the character-attached form of the same SpritePackValue hub used by standalone packs. The formats reference documents external field coverage; pack import instead normalizes supported files into the canonical studio shape, without claiming a foreign field schema.
